Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the intro form at last week's ISV forum — CloudBridge is excited to get Redwood onto our AWS SellWith pathway. Before we start the listing work, our Marketplace ops team needs clarity on two items that commonly block approvals:

1) Listing visibility / entitlement mapping: how will you expose SKU-level availability for cross-account sellwith claims (resale/sellwith)? We need a short description of the authz surface so our entitlement engine can evaluate.

2) Evidence & upload flow: we typically require a technical evidence bundle (connector auth proof, telemetry sampling, and a billing metering mapping). Please share the expected artifact format and any small-scope samples you can provide.

I attached our integration spec (PDF) and a checklist to speed the intake. Can we run a 45-minute joint session next week to align on minimal data elements for an initial pilot? Suggested times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

If it helps, the pilot could scope only a single SKU (sandbox) to validate entitlement visibility to a reseller.

Thanks,
--
Priya Reddy
Head of Partnerships, CloudBridge Solutions
priya@cloudbridge.com
+1 415-555-0118

Hi Priya — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear checklist.

We can absolutely run a pilot. High-level answers below; happy to dive into details on the call.

- Entitlement visibility: Redwood will expose SKU entitlement via a dedicated Catalog API endpoint that returns SKU availability scoped to a customer account id + sellwith_token. For the pilot we can implement a simple mapping: SKUs -> partner_offer_id -> allowed_reseller_ids. The endpoint supports query params for region and tier so you can filter programmatically.

- Evidence & upload: we typically accept a ZIP with a small manifest: connector_auth.json, sample_metering.csv, and a short README.md. For faster review we can also link a Drive folder (see HubSpot record) and provide a signed attestation for telemetry sampling.

Next steps I propose:
1) Joint call Tue 29 Aug 10:30 PT (Ben will cover metering; Olga should join for auth details)
2) We prepare a 1-SKU sandbox mapping and a small evidence ZIP (we'll upload a stub to the Drive link you provided)
3) CloudBridge shares any additional marketplace gating questions ahead of the call

Looping in Olga and Ben so they get visibility.

Cheers,
--
Marcus Lin
Head of Ecosystem Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Marcus / Ben — forwarding Priya's note and our quick technical read. High-level items we should prepare before Tue's call: 

- Minimal API contract (OpenAPI snippet): I can draft a 2-endpoint surface: /catalog/sku-visibility (GET) and /catalog/entitlement-mapping (POST) for pilot. The GET will return JSON with fields: sku_id, partner_offer_id, allowed_resellers [id], effective_from, effective_to.

- Auth model: OAuth2 client credentials for the partner->redwood catalog query, and a short-lived sellwith_token for final reseller claim. We should confirm whether CloudBridge requires role-based scopes or will accept a single read scope for the pilot.

- Metering sample: Ben, pls confirm the columns you need for trial mapping (timestamp, sku, tokens_consumed, customer_id, invoice_reference). If we can provide a 24-hour sample snapshot it should be enough for their evidence team.

- Compliance ask: CloudBridge asked about a signed attestation. We have a template but legal will want to review. Recommend we mark attestation as "provider-asserted" with an option to add a brief SOC2 excerpt if they escalate.

I'll attach a draft OpenAPI snippet and a README stub to the Drive link Marcus put in the HubSpot note.

Olga
